source_refs.note: Exercise 12.2, Question 2 (i)-(ii): continuity of piecewise functions at x = c (book p.233). Answer key PDF 310 wrongly says (i) is discontinuous at x = 2.

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Discuss the continuity of \(f(x)\) at \(x = c\): \[f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 5, & x \le 2 \\ 4x + 1, & x > 2 \end{cases}\]\(c = 2\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh continuity (lagataar hona) ka sawal hai. Function do tukron (pieces) mein diya gaya hai aur formula \(x = 2\) par badalta hai.
Humein dekhna hai ke dono tukre \(x = 2\) par aapas mein jur'te hain ya graph wahan toot'ta hai.
Plan: \(f(2)\), LHL aur RHL nikalenge, phir teeno shartein check karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x \le 2\) ke liye \(f(x) = 2x + 5\), aur \(x > 2\) ke liye \(f(x) = 4x + 1\); \(c = 2\).
Humein find karna hai: kya \(f\) point \(x = 2\) par continuous hai?
Tareeqa: \(f\) point \(x = c\) par continuous (lagataar, bina toote) tab hota hai jab teen shartein poori hon: (i) \(f(c)\) defined ho, (ii) \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x)\) exist kare yani LHL = RHL, (iii) yeh limit \(f(c)\) ke barabar ho. Agar ek bhi shart toot jaye to \(f\) wahan discontinuous hai. Aasaan zubaan mein: graph ko us point par qalam uthaye baghair bana sakein to continuous.

Shart (i): \(f(2)\) nikalein
\[f(2) = 2(2) + 5 = 9\]
Kyun: Pehle tukre ke saath \(\le\) ka nishaan hai, yani "chhota ya barabar". Is liye \(x = 2\) khud pehle tukre \(2x + 5\) mein aata hai.
Dhyan dein: Hamesha inequality ke nishaan dekh kar faisla karein ke \(x = c\) kis tukre mein hai; ghalat tukra lene se poora jawab ghalat ho jata hai.

Left hand limit nikalein
\[\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 2^-} (2x + 5)\]
\[= 4 + 5 = 9\]
Kyun: 2 se pehle (1.9, 1.99) \(x < 2\) hai, is liye pehla tukra \(2x + 5\) lagega.

Right hand limit nikalein
\[\lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 2^+} (4x + 1)\]
\[= 8 + 1 = 9\]
Kyun: 2 ke baad (2.1, 2.01) \(x > 2\) hai, is liye doosra tukra \(4x + 1\) lagega.

Shart (ii): kya limit exist karti hai?
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 9\]
\[\lim_{x \to 2} f(x) = 9\]
Kyun: Dono taraf se function ek hi value 9 ki taraf ja raha hai, is liye limit exist karti hai.

Shart (iii): limit ko \(f(2)\) se milayein
\[\lim_{x \to 2} f(x) = 9 = f(2)\]
Kyun: Teeno shartein poori ho gayin. Matlab dono seedhi lines (straight lines) point \((2, 9)\) par aa kar mil jati hain; graph mein koi gap ya jump nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[f(1.99) = 3.98 + 5 = 8.98\]
\[f(2.01) = 8.04 + 1 = 9.04\]
Kyun: 2 ke dono taraf values 9 ke qareeb hain, aur \(f(2)\) bhi 9 hai. Is liye function wahan continuous hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(f\) point \(x = 2\) par continuous hai (LHL \(=\) RHL \(= f(2) = 9\))

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein likha hai "(i) \(f\) is discontinuous at \(x = 2\)". Yeh ghalat hai: \(f(2) = 9\), left hand limit \(2(2) + 5 = 9\) aur right hand limit \(4(2) + 1 = 9\) hai, yani teeno shartein poori hain. Sahi jawab: \(f\) point \(x = 2\) par continuous hai.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Discuss the continuity of \(f(x)\) at \(x = c\): \[f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 1, & x < 1 \\ 4, & x = 1 \\ 2x, & x > 1 \end{cases}\]\(c = 1\)
blocks.explanation:
Is function ke teen hisse hain: \(x < 1\) ka formula, \(x = 1\) par alag se di gayi value, aur \(x > 1\) ka formula.
Humein dekhna hai ke \(x = 1\) par function continuous hai ya nahi.
Aise sawal mein aksar dono taraf ki limit to barabar hoti hai, lekin beech wali value alag rakh di jati hai. Is liye teesri shart bohat ghaur se check karni hai.
Plan: \(f(1)\), LHL, RHL nikalein aur teeno shartein dekhein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x < 1\) ke liye \(f(x) = 3x - 1\), \(f(1) = 4\), aur \(x > 1\) ke liye \(f(x) = 2x\); \(c = 1\).
Humein find karna hai: kya \(f\) point \(x = 1\) par continuous hai?
Tareeqa: \(f\) point \(x = c\) par continuous (lagataar, bina toote) tab hota hai jab teen shartein poori hon: (i) \(f(c)\) defined ho, (ii) \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x)\) exist kare yani LHL = RHL, (iii) yeh limit \(f(c)\) ke barabar ho. Agar ek bhi shart toot jaye to \(f\) wahan discontinuous hai. Aasaan zubaan mein: graph ko us point par qalam uthaye baghair bana sakein to continuous.

Shart (i): \(f(1)\) nikalein
\[f(1) = 4\]
Kyun: Beech wali line seedha batati hai ke bilkul \(x = 1\) par function ki value 4 hai. Yahan kisi formula mein value rakhne ki zaroorat nahi.

Left hand limit nikalein
\[\lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^-} (3x - 1)\]
\[= 3 - 1 = 2\]
Kyun: 1 se pehle \(x < 1\) hai, is liye pehla formula \(3x - 1\) lagega.

Right hand limit nikalein
\[\lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^+} 2x\]
\[= 2(1) = 2\]
Kyun: 1 ke baad \(x > 1\) hai, is liye teesra formula \(2x\) lagega.

Shart (ii): kya limit exist karti hai?
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 2\]
\[\lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = 2\]
Kyun: Dono taraf se function 2 ki taraf ja raha hai, is liye limit exist karti hai aur 2 hai.

Shart (iii): limit ko \(f(1)\) se milayein
\[\lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = 2\]
\[f(1) = 4\]
\[2 \ne 4\]
Kyun: Limit 2 hai lekin function ki asal value 4 hai, is liye teesri shart toot gayi. Graph ki line point \((1, 2)\) ki taraf aati hai lekin wahan ek khaali sa sooraakh (hole) hai, aur function ka point upar \((1, 4)\) par alag para hai.
Dhyan dein: Sirf LHL = RHL dekh kar "continuous" likh dena aam ghalti hai. Limit ka exist karna kaafi nahi; limit ko \(f(c)\) ke barabar bhi hona chahiye.

Tasdeeq
\[f(0.99) = 2.97 - 1 = 1.97\]
\[f(1.01) = 2.02\]
Kyun: 1 ke qareeb values 2 ki taraf ja rahi hain, 4 ki taraf nahi. Agar kitab \(f(1) = 2\) rakhti to function continuous hota.
blocks.final_answer: \(f\) point \(x = 1\) par discontinuous hai (limit 2 hai lekin \(f(1) = 4\))
